physicalNotes: Radius 0.23552502 Jupiter radii from Livingston et al. 2018 (2018AJ....156...78L), via the NASA Exoplanet Archive (https://ui.adsabs.harvard.edu/abs/2018AJ....156...78L/abstract): 16,838.2 km at 71,492 km per Jupiter radius. GM from the mass 0.0235 Jupiter masses (the NASA Exoplanet Archive's calculated value (M-R relationship, its Chen & Kipping 2017 mass-radius relationship): a model, not a measurement, via the NASA Exoplanet Archive, https://exoplanetarchive.ipac.caltech.edu/docs/pscp_calc.html) times JPL's Jupiter GM. A sphere: no oblateness is measured.

sources.period: Livingston et al. 2018 (2018AJ....156...78L), via the NASA Exoplanet Archive ps table (pl_refname LIVINGSTON_ET_AL__2018): P 10.06049 d
sources.shape: Livingston et al. 2018 (2018AJ....156...78L), via the NASA Exoplanet Archive ps table (pl_refname LIVINGSTON_ET_AL__2018): a/R* 19.1; Mayo et al. 2018 (2018AJ....155..136M), via the NASA Exoplanet Archive ps table (pl_refname MAYO_ET_AL__2018): inclination 88.40454 degrees

sources.phase: Livingston et al. 2018 (2018AJ....156...78L), via the NASA Exoplanet Archive ps table (pl_refname LIVINGSTON_ET_AL__2018): transit mid-time 2457590.4834 BJD, taken as BJD_TDB; with its period, the row that predicts 2026-01-01 best (1 sigma 662 min)
sources.orientation: Display convention: transit photometry does not measure the orbit's position angle on the sky, so the ascending node is set at position angle 0 (celestial north).
